reach.rationale: No experimental, preview, RC or canary APIs at all; the only reach is one recently-stable decorator (@Service, v22, ~5 months old) in the central data service, plus stable-since-v19/20 idioms elsewhere.

evidence: app/src/app/data/page-data.ts:48 — single @Service use; semantically identical to @Injectable({providedIn: 'root'}), a one-line swap
app/src/app/page-title-strategy.ts:9 — the one other service sticks to long-stable @Injectable()
grep over app/src — no experimental markers (unstable_/experimental_), no zone.js, no preview flags in app/angular.json
containment.rationale: The single newest API is one decorator on one class with a mechanical fallback; everything else in the 28 source files is long-stable, so there is effectively nothing to contain.

evidence: app/src/app/app.config.server.ts:11-13 — provideServerRendering/withRoutes is the only non-deprecated way to configure v22 SSR (provideServerRouting removed); provideAppInitializer replaces deprecated APP_INITIALIZER
app/src/app/pages/not-found/not-found.ts:14-17 — RESPONSE_INIT is the documented stable way to emit a 404 status for SSR, a real correctness need
app/src/app/pages/home/home.ts:32-34 — linkedSignal is the exact-fit tool for 'follow the URL unless the user is mid-typing', avoiding an effect+manual-sync dance
app/src/app/pages/pokemon/move-table.ts:84-87 — linkedSignal resets user sort when the table (source signal) changes; justified use of source-reset semantics
app/src/app/pages/home/home.html (native controls) — deliberately avoids v22's Signal Forms, using plain form elements where nothing fancier is needed
justification.rationale: Every newer API is the current stable recommendation for the job (SSR setup, response status, URL-synced ephemeral state), and the app shows restraint by not adopting v22's preview features (@boundary, Navigation API, injectAsync) it had no need for.

findings.issue: @Service() is the newest API in the framework (stable only since v22.0, June 2026) and sits in the central data/hydration service; its semantics could still be refined in v23+
findings.suggestion: Keep it (it is the officially recommended style with an automatic migration), but the fallback @Injectable({providedIn: 'root'}) is a one-line swap if it ever changes

findings.issue: @angular/forms is declared as a dependency but no forms API (FormsModule, NgModel, FormControl) is imported anywhere in the app
findings.suggestion: Remove the unused dependency to shrink install surface

findings.issue: AngularNodeAppEngine({ allowedHosts: ['*'] }) disables the SSRF host allow-list; a stable (not experimental) option, but a security-sensitive default being overridden
findings.suggestion: The inline comment justifies it (no Host-derived requests), but consider making the public host configurable via env var instead of a blanket wildcard

summary: This app takes almost no experimental risk: zero experimental, preview, RC or canary APIs, and it avoids v22's preview features (@boundary, Navigation API, injectAsync) entirely. Its one very-new dependency is the @Service() decorator, stable only since v22.0 (June 2026) but semantically identical to @Injectable({providedIn: 'root'}) and confined to a single class. Everything else rests on APIs stable since v19–v21, each of which is the current recommended replacement for deprecated predecessors.
